seo.title: TablePro vs TablePlus: features and licensing
seo.description: Two native database clients with Mac, iPhone and iPad apps: compare platforms, prices, AI and MCP, and importing your TablePlus connections into TablePro.

header.title: TablePro vs TablePlus
header.lead: TablePlus and TablePro are native database clients. Compare their free features, licensing and supported platforms. They are separate products from unrelated makers.

tablepro: An open-source client, including the code of paid features.
A free app with no tab or window limits. Paid plans add {starterExamples}.
A free iPhone and iPad app with no in-app purchases.

glance.intro: Both clients have an AI chat, an MCP server, a schema diagram and Excel export. TablePlus added its MCP server, its diagram and Excel export in version {cells.mcp.version}, released {cells.mcp.date}.

diagram.label: Schema diagram
diagram.tablepro: A read-only ER diagram, exported as PNG or SQL

excelExport.label: Export to Excel
excelExport.tablepro: Free, alongside CSV, JSON, SQL and other formats

safeMode.label: Safe Mode
safeMode.tablepro: Per connection, from Silent to Read-Only, with Touch ID on the stricter levels

items.text: It lists engines that TablePro does not support, such as Vertica and Greenplum.
It is available through Setapp, if that is how you get your Mac apps.
It runs on older systems: macOS {mac.minVersion} and iOS {cells.ios.value} are enough, where TablePro needs newer versions of both.
TablePro is open source under the AGPLv3, including the code of its paid features. TablePlus is closed source.

The free app connects to every supported engine and includes the AI assistant, the MCP server and Safe Mode, with no tab or window limits. <link>Paid plans</link> add features such as {starterExamples}.
The iPhone and iPad app is free, with no in-app purchases and no license. The TablePlus iPhone app has in-app purchases, or comes with a TablePlus license.

<link>iCloud Sync</link> syncs connections across Macs, iPhones and iPads. It requires Starter on the Mac and is free on iPhone and iPad. TablePlus syncs its connections through a cloud folder you choose, such as Dropbox or iCloud.
Team plans add <link>{teamExamples}</link> for sharing connections and saved queries with your team.
TablePro’s separate <link>iPhone and iPad app</link> has fewer features than the Mac app: no AI assistant, MCP server or autocomplete.
TablePro is not a schema designer: its ER diagram is a read-only snapshot of the current schema.
TablePlus licenses keep working after their year of updates. TablePro one-time purchases do not expire. TablePro subscriptions lock paid features when they end; the free app keeps working.

switching.intro: Import TablePlus connections, including the Setapp edition’s. TablePlus can stay closed, and its files are not changed.
steps: In TablePro, choose <ui>File > Import > Import from Other App…</ui>
Select TablePlus. Turn on <ui>Include passwords</ui> to read saved passwords from the macOS Keychain.
macOS asks for your login password once for each saved password. Choose <ui>Always Allow</ui> on each prompt.

Review the list, decide what happens to any duplicates, and click <ui>Import</ui>. Groups, SSH tunnels and connection colors come across. A connection to an engine TablePro does not support arrives unchecked.
Before you remove TablePlus, open a connection that had a password to check that it came across.
after: Saved queries, query history and keyboard shortcuts stay in TablePlus.
A connection set to ask for its password every time arrives set to prompt for the password.

faq.question: Can I keep using TablePlus after importing?
faq.answer: Yes. The import only reads TablePlus’s connection files, so both apps keep working with their own copies.

faq.question: How does TablePro’s speed compare with TablePlus?
faq.answer: No reproducible benchmark is cited here. Performance depends on the query, database, network and computer; native architecture alone does not establish a speed advantage.

notes.tableplus-free-limits: No time limit, but at most {value} open tabs, {value} windows and {value} advanced filters at a time
notes.tableplus-one-year-updates: Paid once, with a year of updates. The app keeps working after that.
notes.tableplus-databases: Relational, document, key-value and analytical engines, among them PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, SQLite, Redis, MongoDB, Oracle, Cassandra, Snowflake, Vertica and Greenplum. Some engines are available on only some platforms.
notes.tableplus-ai: A chat plugin that works with OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub Copilot or a local model
notes.tableplus-ios-purchase: Free to download, with in-app purchases. An active TablePlus license also covers it on a set number of devices. It needs iOS {value} or later.
notes.tableplus-sync-folder: Connections sync through a cloud folder you choose, such as Dropbox or iCloud
